text:
Ashley: Anyone else hitting a weird redwoodctl auth/login issue after a macOS upgrade? Starts the browser device flow but never writes ~/.redwood/profiles.json, then `redwoodctl local serve` fails with 401.
Kevin: I saw something like that after updating Homebrew packages. What does `redwoodctl version` show?
Ashley: v0.12.3
Kevin: Hm. Do you have any launchd/launchctl jobs for redwoodctl or a credential helper running? Could be a race with the keychain.
Jules: Can you paste the last ~20 lines from `~/.redwood/debug.log` (or a minimal redacted snippet)?
Ashley: sure, pasted below:
```
2024-11-08T09:12:03Z auth: starting browser flow
2024-11-08T09:12:10Z auth: browser flow completed, got code
2024-11-08T09:12:10Z auth: token refresh failed: unauthorized
2024-11-08T09:12:10Z fs: open /Users/ashley/.redwood/profiles.json: permission denied
2024-11-08T09:12:10Z fs: fallback to default profile
```
Kevin: permission denied + token unauthorized smells like the file is owned by root. Did you run the installer with sudo by any chance?
Ashley: oh god yes i used `sudo installer` to avoid the "permission" prompt earlier. Didn't think about where files end up.
Sam: that'll do it. Installer creates ~/.redwood with the invoking user's $HOME if run normally, but with sudo the owner becomes root and the per-user launchagent can't write.
Sam: Quick workaround:
```
sudo chown -R $(whoami):$(id -gn) ~/.redwood
# then reinit auth
redwoodctl auth login --reinit
# if you use the launch agent
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.redwoodctl.auth.plist || true
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.redwoodctl.auth.plist || true
```
Ashley: chown + login --reinit fixed it, thanks :tada:
Ashley: one follow-up: CI runners that use a root-created home or baked images with ~/.redwood as root will hit this. We should detect this in the installer and refuse sudo, or at least warn.
Jules: Agreed. File a GH issue? We can add an installer check for UID==0 and print a clear message explaining why it's bad and how to fix.
Kevin: Also add a postinstall step that detects launchd plist ownership and rewrites to the user when appropriate.
oncall-bot: Incident created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/5123 — "installer: warn/error when run with sudo; document chown flow" (priority: medium)
Sam: I'll pick this up and draft a small CLI guard + docs blurb.
Ashley: great, thanks everyone — feel free to close this thread once the GH issue has a PR link.
